msItem.title: Amores 3.10

handDesc.handNote: Main text and any darker interventions are distinguished where observed. No individual historical correcting hands are inferred from tonal contrast in monochrome photographs.

origin.p: The supplied BnF IIIF manifest dates the manuscript to 1001–1100. The catalogue dating is not a date assigned to individual interventions.

surrogates.p: The original full-resolution digital images and enlarged crops were inspected for this first pass. Gallica source reuse conditions apply. No text was populated from LL or another witness.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded first reading of all 48 annotated verse positions, with manuscript-specific spellings and observed interventions. Independent second reading is required before integration as reviewed.

correction.p: No silent emendation from an edition or another witness. Local uncertain letters use unclear, irrecoverable text or signs use gap. Observed above-line letters use add. Tonal distinctions use hi without an invented underlying erased text or historical hand. Manuscript annotations use note type manuscript, distinct from editorial evidence notes.

normalization.p: One source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs, long s, and capitals are represented in legible Latin types. Word boundaries are editorially segmented; no indentation whitespace is inserted inside verse mixed content. Selected ligatures and abbreviation signs are declared typographic approximations; explicit expansions remain in TEI rather than a separate reading mode. This is not a facsimile-perfect inventory of every minute stroke.

punctuation.p: Significant observed punctuation is retained schematically, without adding systematic modern sentence punctuation.

segmentation.p: Each l represents a verse and physical written line at its canonical poem position. Elegiac couplets are editorial grouping. Indentation is encoded only where the inspected source layout supports an offset; it is not inferred automatically from verse parity. Page breaks follow the photographed left/right physical pages. Facsimile zones reproduce the existing annotation rectangles unchanged; they may include neighbouring ink and exclude marginal annotations.

interpretation.p: First-pass evidence notes are a working queue for an independent agent, not assignments for the human editor. Genuine source uncertainty remains local; consequential unresolved interpretation is distinguished from ordinary observation.

revisionDesc.change: Completed first reading from source images and enlarged crops, with line coverage and evidence notes. Independent second reading not yet performed.

lg.l: Annua uenerunt cerealis tempora sacri
Secubat in uacuo sola puella toro
Flaua ceres tenues spicis redimita capillos
Cur inhibes sacris commoda nostra tuis
Te dea munificam gentes ubique loquuntur
Nec minus humanis inuidet illa bonis
Ante nec hirsutis ornabat farra colonis
Nec notum terris area nomen erat
Glandiferas quercus oracula prima ferebant
Hoc erat &et teneri cespitis herba cibus
Prima ceres docuit turgescere semen in agris
Prima coloratas subsecuitque comas
Prima iugis tauros supponere colla coegit
Et ueterem curuo dente reuellit humum
Hanc quisquam lacrimis &et tristitia
Et bene tormentis secubituque coli
Nec tamen est quāquamuis agros amet illa feraces
Rustica nec uiduum pectus amoris habet
Cretes erunt testes nec fingunt omnia cretes
Crete nutrito terra superba ioui
Illic sideream mundi qui temperat arcem
Exiguus tenero lac bibit ore puer
Magna fides testi testis laudatur alumno
Fassuram cererem crimina nostra puto
Viderat iasium cretea diua sub ida
Figentem certa terga ferina manu
Vidit &et ut tenere flammam rapuere medulle
Hinc pudor ex illa parte trahebat amor
Victus amore pudor sulcos ardere uideres
Et sata cum minima parte redire sui
Cum bene iactatos pulsarant arua ligones
Ruperat &et durum uomer aduncus humum
Seminaque in latos ierant equaliter agros
Irrita decepti uota colentis erant
Diua potens frugum siluis cessabat in altis
Deciderant longe spicea serta come
Sola crete fecundo fertilist anno
Omnia qua tulerat se dea messis erat
Ipsa locus nemorum canebat frugibus ide
Et ferus in silua farra metebat aper
Optauit minos similes sibi legis in annos

l.unclear: Optasset cereris longus ut esset amor

lg.l: Quod tibi secubitus tristes dea flaua fuissent
Hoc ego cur sacris nunc cogor inesse tuis
Cur ego sim tristis cum sit tibi nata reperta
Regnaque quam iuno sorte minore regat
Festa dies ueneremque uocat cantusque merumque
Hec decet ad dominos munera ferre deos

div.head: First-pass evidence notes
div.note: The first two written lines after3.9 are the opening couplet of3.10, not a heading. The large flourished A begins Annua. All48canonical verses are present. Full opening images95and96 show a modest alternating offset, with protruding odd-verse initials and later even-verse starts; indentation here records that observed layout rather than an automatic rule from verse parity.
The manuscript writes ceres with initial c and redimita in the opening address. Small darker marks below the latter word are visible, but no erased letter or historical hand is inferred.
Munificam is faded and compressed, with small marks above the initial part. The provisional reading is kept local in unclear.
The word after Nec is provisionally notum; its internal minims are faded. The remainder terris area nomen erat is legible.

The enlarged G is offset into the margin and slightly above its line. The following landiferas is faint; the provisional combined reading Glandiferas remains uncertain locally. Quercus oracula prima ferebant follows in that order.
The et ligature is encoded with a schematic glyph and explicit expansion. Cespitis is retained without normalization.
The visible wording is Prima coloratas subsecuitque comas.
The lower part of image95 left is faded. Iugis and supponere colla coegit are provisional readings; no letters are supplied from a different witness.
The middle phrase ueterem curuo dente is faint. Reuellit humum is clearer at the line end and retained with that ending.

Image95 right starts Hanc quisquam lacrimis with an et ligature. Tristitia is tentative and the line ending is too faint for a secure reading. The local gap denotes illegible ink within this surviving verse, not manuscript absence.
A horizontal stroke abbreviates the nasal in quamuis. The visible qua with stroke is expanded quam before the separately written uis portion.
Cretes appears twice in the verse; the following line begins Crete. These source forms are retained.
The source repeats testi testis and ends laudatur alumno.
The name after Viderat is provisionally iasium; its initial and medial strokes are faded. Cretea diua sub ida is more legible and is not normalized to another spelling.
The source uses plain-e forms tenere and medulle in the visible text. No ae is supplied.
The visible phrase is Hinc pudor ex illa parte trahebat amor.
The verb is provisionally pulsarant. Surface mottling crosses its internal letters, so the form remains unclear locally.
The opening Irrita decepti is faded; the remainder uota colentis erant is more legible.
Spicea serta come is retained with plain e in the final word.

The faded opening appears Sola crete; its complete letter sequence is uncertain and the encoding does not assert a demonstrable omission of any expected word. Fertilis is also uncertain. A darker above-line sign resembling t is separately recorded as a manuscript annotation because its exact relationship to the base letters is not secure.
The visible sequence is Omnia qua tulerat se dea messis erat.
The manuscript reads Ipsa locus nemorum canebat frugibus ide. The visible place-name form ide is retained.
The opening is provisionally Optauit. The word between sibi and in annos appears legis but is faint; no normalized alternative is imposed.
The entire last line on image95 right is very faded. Optasset cereris longus ut esset amor is only a provisional reading and remains unclear.

Image96 left continues with an uncertain opening form Quod and the legible tibi secubitus tristes dea flaua fuissent. A small mark over the opening is visible, but its abbreviation function is not asserted.
The short word provisionally read cur in the opening Hoc ego cur is faint. The remainder sacris nunc cogor inesse tuis is legible.
The poem ends with Hec decet ad dominos munera ferre deos. The next large M and its separate marginal annotation mark the following poem, outside the48verses of3.10.
